s-commonwealth.who: Citizens of listed Commonwealth countries. Nepal is not a Commonwealth member and is not on the eligible country list for the Master and PhD rounds, so Nepali citizens cannot apply.
s-commonwealth.how: Nothing to apply for as a Nepali citizen. Look at Chevening, a university scholarship or another route listed for the UK.

s-holland.name: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship)
s-holland.covers: EUR 5,000 one time grant paid in the first year of study. It is not a full tuition award
s-holland.who: Non-EEA students (Nepal qualifies) starting a full time bachelor or master programme at a participating Dutch university, who do not already hold a Dutch degree
s-holland.how: Apply through the university, not a central office. There is no single national deadline: each institution sets its own, usually 1 February or 1 May, and applications open about 1 November. Check that your programme is on the university list.

hu.work: A student residence permit lets you work up to 24 hours a week in term and full time in official breaks (up to 90 days or 66 working days a year), with no separate work permit. You need a Hungarian tax number and your employer must register the job. Pay covers daily costs, not tuition.

cn.work: A study residence permit is not a work permit. Off campus work study or an internship needs your university approval and the employer and period written on your residence permit before you start. In term work study is generally limited to 8 hours a week and 40 hours a month, and in vacations to 16 hours a week and 80 hours a month. Ordinary jobs, freelancing and business are not allowed on a student permit.

bim.name: BITM (formerly BIM, Bachelor of Information Technology Management)
bim.about_add: TU renamed BIM to BITM from the 2082/83 session. A section takes 33 students (30 regular and 3 scholarship seats). Shanker Dev Campus has 66 seats.

bsc-csit.about_add: For 2083 TU allotted 3,108 seats in 61 colleges, 80 percent open and 20 percent Samabesi (inclusive).

bca.about_add: More than 125 colleges run TU BCA and every one admits through the same FoHSS entrance exam.

faq_add.q: How many BSc CSIT seats are there, and which colleges?
faq_add.a: TU Institute of Science and Technology allotted 3,108 BSc CSIT seats for 2083 across 61 colleges: 16 TU campuses with 1,224 seats and 45 private colleges with 1,884. In every college 80 percent of seats are open and 20 percent are the Samabesi (inclusive) quota, meant for students who studied Grades 8 to 12 in a government or community school. Patan Multiple Campus and Amrit Campus are the biggest with 144 each, then Bhairahawa Multiple Campus with 108. Most private colleges take 36 or 48. After the entrance result you rank up to 10 colleges on the IoST portal and TU publishes the list. Seats change each year, so check the IoST notice.

faq_add.q: Which colleges run TU BCA and how do I get in?
faq_add.a: More than 125 colleges run the TU BCA: 15 TU campuses plus private and community colleges in the Valley and in Biratnagar, Itahari, Damak, Janakpur, Hetauda, Bharatpur, Butwal, Dang, Nepalgunj, Surkhet and Mahendranagar. Students from any stream can apply with at least a D grade in every subject of Grades 11 and 12 and a CGPA of 1.8, or a second division in +2 (2083 notice). Admission is by the TU Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences entrance exam, which was held on 16 August 2026 with a fee of NPR 1,500, and a re-entrance exam followed on 19 September 2026 because many colleges had empty seats. A college usually admits one batch of about 35.

Yes. From the 2082/83 session Tribhuvan University renamed the Bachelor of Information Management (BIM) as the Bachelor of Information Technology Management (BITM). A section takes 33 students, 30 regular and 3 scholarship seats (a compulsory 10 percent). Shanker Dev Campus, the TU campus, has 66 seats. Entry is the CMAT exam of the Faculty of Management and at least a D+ (CGPA 1.8) in Grades 11 and 12.

faq_add.q: Can Nepali students apply for the Commonwealth Scholarship?
faq_add.a: No. Nepal is not a Commonwealth member and is not on the eligible country list for the Commonwealth Master and PhD scholarships, which list countries such as Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Several websites still say Nepal is eligible, so do not pay any agent for it. For the UK look at Chevening and at scholarships offered by the university itself.

It is a one time grant of EUR 5,000 paid in the first year to non-EEA students, so Nepali students qualify, who start a full time bachelor or master programme at a participating Dutch university. It is not full funding. You apply through the university, each one sets its own deadline (usually 1 February or 1 May) and its own rules, and applications open about 1 November. You cannot have a Dutch degree already.

faq_add.q: How many hours can I work while studying in Hungary or China?
faq_add.a: Hungary lets a student residence permit holder work up to 24 hours a week in term and full time in official breaks, without a separate work permit, once you hold a Hungarian tax number. China is much stricter: a study permit is not a work permit, off campus work study needs university approval and a note on your residence permit first, and the usual limit is 8 hours a week and 40 hours a month in term. Never start work before the paperwork is done.

faq_add.q: How do I choose a +2 college?
faq_add.a: Check three things before you look at rankings. First, that the college is approved by the National Examination Board for the stream you want, because not every college runs Science, Management, Humanities and Law. Second, ask for the full fee list in writing: admission, monthly, lab, uniform, exam and bus fees add up beyond the headline figure. Third, look at how many seats the stream has, how many students pass the NEB exam, and how far it is from home. Rankings online are mostly advertising.

fa-3.a: Government and embassy scholarships such as Chevening, Fulbright, DAAD, MEXT, GKS, Australia Awards, Eiffel, SISGP, VLIR-UOS and ADB-JSP open every year, plus university scholarships. The Commonwealth Scholarship is not open to Nepali citizens because Nepal is not a Commonwealth member. Deadlines are fixed, so note them six to nine months early.
